statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.excerpt: CLEAN WATER PRIORITY - Give incentives to our farmers to use proven solutions that address agricultural runoff and water contamination.
statements.notes: The summary says the specific items (refundable deep-banding credits, buffer-strip aid, more monitoring) are not on his campaign site. That holds up: the policy page has only the general incentive line above. Searches found no deep-banding source. A search snippet credited to a Daily Signal piece ('Zach Lahn's Plan to Help Farmers While Cleaning Up Iowa's Water', dailysignal.com/?p=235033) says he would incentivize buffer strips through rural funding, but that page returned 403, so it is unverified. Possible source for the buffer-strip item only.

Exact quote not found. A search snippet attributed similar wording to Lahn, 'they're drinking the water too, and they want to do what's right', about working with farmers on drinking water. The snippet did not clearly show which result it came from (possibly newsfromthestates.com/node/410308, an Iowa Capital Dispatch republication, which blocks fetches, or KCRG 2026-04-18). The KCRG Dubuque town hall article I loaded does not contain it; it only has him pledging to work 'alongside' farmers. Unverified.

statements.sourceTitle: This Iowa Democrat is stirring hopes of a red-state comeback by charting his own path
statements.excerpt: a bow-hunting, scripture-quoting, plaid-shirt wearing father of two
statements.notes: Hunter: supported. Gun owner: a search snippet says Sand 'owns two SIG Sauer handguns, goes deer hunting each fall', but I did not identify or load that source page, and the CNN article does not mention guns. Nothing found on the 2021 permitless-carry posts.

statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.exactWording: End tax credits and economic development funds for out-of-state and foreign corporations and prioritize Iowa-based companies with deep community roots.
statements.excerpt: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR IOWA-OWNED COMPANIES - End tax credits and economic development funds for out-of-state and foreign corporations and prioritize Iowa-based companies with deep community roots.
statements.notes: The quote is the first clause of a longer sentence. Context worth adding: search snippets from an Iowa Capital Dispatch republication (newsfromthestates.com/node/430128, 403, not loaded) say Lahn told reporters the line targets companies like Chinese-owned Syngenta, not large projects like the foreign-owned Mesabi Metallics steel mill, which he supports as a 'once in a lifetime' exception. Unverified by direct load.

statements.sourceTitle: How Rob Sand answered voter's question about Iowa steel plant deal
statements.publisher: KTTC / Gray Media Iowa State Capitol Bureau (Dave Price)
statements.excerpt: Lahn's spokesman said Lahn views the project as "transformational" and that "any incentives should be strictly tied to performance, and to the number of Iowans who work there."
statements.notes: 'Transformational' is supported but came through a spokesman (search snippets say he has 'repeatedly' called it that). 'Refocus the Iowa Economic Development Authority' was not found. The campaign page heading 'ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR IOWA-OWNED COMPANIES' (zachlahn.com/policy/) backs the Iowa-owned focus but does not name IEDA. Excerpt paraphrased by the fetch tool. Exact wording should be rechecked before quoting.

statements.sourceTitle: Iowa governor candidates debate incentives for planned steel mill
statements.publisher: ScrapMonster (industry news aggregator; original outlet not credited in fetched text)
statements.exactWording: We don't want a lot of upfront incentives. Instead, we should make sure that this company is making the investments
statements.excerpt: "We don't want a lot of upfront incentives. Instead, we should make sure that this company is making the investments"
statements.notes: The wording differs: 'We don't want a lot of upfront incentives,' not 'We don't want to see a lot of upfront incentives.' A search snippet gives the fuller version: '...improving the infrastructure in Iowa, actually building here, and after meeting benchmarks, then seeing incentives come in after that.' The search engine tied the quote to the KTTC/WOWT/Dakota News Now piece 'How Rob Sand answered voter's question...' but the KTTC copy I loaded does not contain 'upfront' (it may be in the video only). ScrapMonster is an aggregator. Find the original outlet before citing it.

statements.sourceTitle: Data Centers - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: As governor, I'd block the use of NDAs on new data centers and make sure these deals happen out in the open.
statements.notes: The NDA ban is supported only for new data-center deals. A general requirement to disclose all state business incentives, and an NDA ban beyond data centers, were not found on robsand.com issue pages. A Telegraph Herald snippet describes the same data-center plan (ban NDAs between corporations and governments). Narrow the summary to data centers.

statements.sourceTitle: Opportunities for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: As governor, I would expand Statewide Work, Statewide Jobs to the government workforce for jobs that can be done anywhere in Iowa, to support economic opportunities in small towns and rural areas.
statements.notes: The program is about where employees live, so state workers can be based in rural communities. The page does not use the word 'remote', but 'jobs that can be done anywhere in Iowa' fits the summary.

statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.excerpt: Increase quota for Iowa residents at University of Iowa and Iowa State University and task them with solving Iowa's cancer and farming crisis.
statements.notes: The page names UI and ISU specifically, not UNI.

statements.sourceTitle: Making Life More Affordable - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: Establish a Prescription Drugs Review Board to help Iowa negotiate lower prescription drug costs... Expand Iowa's 'Surprise Bill' law to cover all medical appointments and procedures
statements.notes: Same page: 'following the recommendations of our PBM audit' and medical debt relief through partnerships such as Undue Medical Debt. The healthier-iowa page adds 'cracking down on Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) that force patients to use only certain pharmacies'. Precise wording: he would expand the existing surprise-bill law, not create a new one, and the board name is 'Prescription Drugs Review Board'.

statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.excerpt: If a teacher is caught pushing a political agenda in the classroom, their teaching license will be revoked, period.
statements.notes: The quoted phrase 'caught pushing a political agenda' matches the page exactly.

statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.excerpt: END TEACHING TO THE TEST - Eliminate or dramatically reduce standardized testing requirements and focus on mastery of skills.
statements.notes: The page says 'mastery of skills'. 'Mastery-based pacing' is a slight extrapolation. AP coverage (snippet only) also mentions 'innovation waivers' from mandatory testing.

statements.sourceTitle: Making Life More Affordable - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.exactWording: the return on investment is 17 to 1 because investing early in our kids' education reduces the likelihood that they will commit crimes and reduces reliance on public assistance
statements.excerpt: Universal all day Pre-K ... Every Iowa child should have access to high-quality Pre-K no matter where they live.
statements.notes: Universal full-day pre-K is supported (the priorities page also says 'universal all day pre-K'). The page does not say outright that it covers 3- and 4-year-olds; it notes 'over half of Iowa kids ages 3-4 don't attend pre-school.' The '$17 for every dollar' quote was not found verbatim; the campaign wording is '17 to 1'.

statements.sourceTitle: Rob Sand says transgender women shouldn't compete in women's sports, campaign could signal party shift
statements.excerpt: Asked on the Simon Conway radio show whether biological males should compete in women's sports, Sand replied: "no"
statements.notes: Excerpt paraphrased by the fetch tool except for the one-word answer. Search snippets (Erin in the Morning, citing Politico) add: 'I just think girls' sports are for girls and boys' sports are for boys.' Not loaded.

statements.sourceTitle: Making Life More Affordable - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: We need to maintain and grow incentives for clean energy that directly saves consumers money. ... Utah's plug-in solar model is a good one to base this off of to help lower energy costs.
statements.notes: Both parts are supported.

statements.sourceTitle: Accountability for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: mandatory prison time for anyone found guilty of stealing over $10,000 in taxpayer dollars
statements.notes: 'Every year' is backed by KCRG (Dave Price), https://www.kcrg.com/2026/01/06/auditor-sand-prison-public-employees-who-steal-tax-money/, dated 2026-01-05: 'For the seventh straight year, Iowa State Auditor Rob Sand... is asking Republicans in the legislature to toughen punishments against some public officials or public employees who steal at least $10,000 in public funds.' The KCRG wording covers public officials and employees; the campaign page says 'anyone'.

statements.sourceTitle: Accountability for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: banning anyone convicted of fraud from doing business with the state

statements.notes: Not found. The full bullet list on zachlahn.com/policy/ has no apprenticeship or trade-school item, and news searches turned up nothing.

statements.sourceTitle: Opportunities for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: Ohio has changed the rules to match the reality for micro-businesses – allowing small businesses to qualify for specialized state and federal programs... for businesses with 10 employees or fewer.
statements.notes: The page cites the 10-or-fewer threshold for program eligibility (training grants, matched savings, small business support), not for cutting red tape. Red-tape language on the same page is about housing permitting, fees and inspections. Better wording: expand access to state programs for micro-businesses with 10 or fewer employees.

statements.sourceTitle: Policy - Zach Lahn for Governor
statements.excerpt: FOCUS ON AFFORDABILITY - Lessening the tax burden on Iowans, food freedom policies and banning Wall Street hedge-funds from buying single family homes will help make life affordable for Iowa families.
statements.notes: The campaign page backs general 'food freedom policies'. No source found for the claim that his first bill would be an 'Iowa first food freedom bill', or for the details on selling locally produced food.

statements.sourceTitle: Accountability for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: limiting statewide elected officeholders to no more than 3 terms in any statewide office, and state legislators to no more than 12 years in the legislature. Plus, no more than a total of 20 years maximum overall
statements.notes: Same page: cognitive tests, a civics test ('should have to pass one to serve'), and annual town halls (20 per year for statewide officials, 5 for legislators). Corroborated by KCRG, 2026-08-06.

statements.sourceTitle: Iowa governor's race puts term limits debate in spotlight
statements.excerpt: In a May interview with the Des Moines Register, Lahn said he supports term limits for "many things" but not for governor... His campaign declined to comment on whether he supports legislative term limits.
statements.notes: Original source: a May 2026 Des Moines Register interview (not loaded). An Iowa Democrats release quotes him: 'I am actually in favor of term limits for most things' (partisan source, not loaded).

statements.sourceTitle: Accountability for All - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: At 78-years-old, we thank them for their service, wish them a happy retirement, and clear the way
statements.notes: KCRG (2026-08-06) says Sand 'remains flexible on the specific age threshold,' so 78 is his stated proposal but not fixed. I did not confirm whether the page applies it to judges as well as elected officials.

statements.sourceTitle: Rob Sand backs Medicaid pay changes for disabled Iowans, proposes ending privatization
statements.excerpt: Sand supports legislation that would remove income and asset limits for employed Iowans with disabilities on Medicaid... Sand stated he would sign the bill if elected
statements.notes: Excerpt paraphrased by the fetch tool. The article names the bill 'Work Without Worry'.

statements.sourceTitle: Making Life More Affordable - Rob Sand for Governor
statements.excerpt: Supporting policies like universal school meals would not only ensure our kids have the fuel they need to pay attention and be productive in the classroom, but would save every Iowa parent time and money each week.
statements.notes: The page says he supports universal school meals rather than laying out a specific plan, so 'supports' is more accurate than 'proposes'.

statements.sourceTitle: Two candidates call for more Iowa-grown food to be served in Iowa schools
statements.excerpt: "I would like to see a time in which 80% of the food served in Iowa's public schools is grown in the state of Iowa."
statements.notes: The 80% Iowa-grown goal is verified on Radio Iowa. The universal free breakfast and lunch quote appeared only in a search-engine summary, credited to a West Des Moines town hall, likely from The 19th (19thnews.org/2026/10/iowa-governors-race-maha-strategy/, which returned 402). I could not load it, so the quote is unverified. Radio Iowa does not contain it.

Not found. Coverage of the emergency-powers bill (Yahoo republication of an Iowa House passage story) quotes Democratic lawmakers saying it targets a possible Democratic governor, but has no statement from Sand. Not on the robsand.com issue pages checked.

statements.notes: Excerpt is fragmentary (elisions from the fetch tool).

statements.sourceTitle: Rob Sand's Plan to Legalize, Tax, and Regulate Adult-use Cannabis
statements.excerpt: Rob would add cannabis experts to the already-existing division [Alcoholic Beverages Division]... Rob would prioritize the issue of grow licenses for small and mid-size family farms
statements.notes: The page says 'small and mid-size family farms', not only small farms. 'Tax' is in the plan title on robsand.com/priorities. The CBS2 'Beyond the Podium' interview (no date shown) also has Sand saying 'we should treat it the way we treat alcohol.'
